findings.label: D3 — GuestHost booking sourceRef is the activity-event ID, not the booking entity ID; identity-semantics decision required
findings.decision: Option 4 — persist artifacts.source_ref = event.EntityID for booking event types and retain event.ID in metadata, coupled to Re-ingestion Option B (update-in-place).

findings.evidence: internal/connector/guesthost/normalizer.go:26 sets sourceRef := event.ID; the business entity is ActivityEvent.EntityID at internal/connector/guesthost/types.go:10; internal/api/context.go:284 looks up a booking ID, with a stale assertion in the comment at :276-277
findings.note: DECIDED as Option 4 (design.md#d3-identity-semantics-decision-decided--option-4) and RATIFIED 2026-07-29 via TR-BUG-019-003-001. Rationale: the consumer contract is expressed in business-entity terms, source_ref is the indexed identity column (idx_artifacts_source), retaining event.ID in metadata preserves audit lineage at zero cost, and every other connector keys source_ref on the stable external entity. Keying on event.ID would force every future consumer to carry an event->entity join the index cannot serve. Option 4 is PROHIBITED without Re-ingestion Option B, because the three booking lifecycle events collide on one ref by design and skip-on-match would freeze bookings in their created state. Ratification is now recorded; Scope 4 is no longer decision-blocked, though it remains unexecuted until a bugfix-fastlane delivery run.

transitionRequests.summary: RATIFICATION REQUESTED (not a blocker). This packet DECIDES D3 as Option 4: persist artifacts.source_ref = event.EntityID for booking event types and retain event.ID in metadata, coupled to Re-ingestion Option B (update-in-place). Options table and full justification: design.md#d3-identity-semantics-decision-decided--option-4. Because the decision has an API-contract consequence (booking.created/updated/cancelled are three events for one booking, which Option 4 collapses to one artifact), the guesthost connector owner and the API contract owner should ratify or overturn it. Scope 4 implements it; Scopes 2-3 are unaffected either way. If overturned, Scope 4 is re-planned.
transitionRequests.resolvedBy: Owner-delegated ratification 2026-07-29; criterion: best long-term option, no shortcuts. Recorded by bubbles.bug on behalf of the operator.
transitionRequests.outcome: RATIFIED AS OPTION 4. artifacts.source_ref carries event.EntityID for booking event types, event.ID is retained in metadata, coupled to Re-ingestion Option B (update-in-place). Option 4 without Option B remains prohibited.
transitionRequests.outcomeRationale: Long-term rationale of record: the consumer contract at internal/api/context.go:284 is expressed in BUSINESS-ENTITY terms (it looks up by booking id). Event IDs are transport artifacts; entity IDs are domain identity. Three events (booking.created / booking.updated / booking.cancelled) collapse to one booking, so the many-to-one relation only resolves when the indexed provenance column is keyed on the entity. Keying on event.ID would require every future consumer to carry an event->entity join that idx_artifacts_source (source_id, source_ref) cannot serve.
